source_behavior: The container scene owns m_pointerPos, uses it for slot selection and the carried item, and snaps a stationary pointer to the slot center.
The source container pointer uses an SD/splitscreen input multiplier of 0.6.
UIScene selects a 480 movie for standard PS3 output and falls back to the 720 movie when that asset is absent.
UIScene uses 5% inset on each edge for the standard 90% safe zone.
IUIScene_CraftingMenu UpdateVerticalSlots keeps only the center variant in standard-definition non-wide mode.
java_port: GLFW window points, framebuffer pixels and scaled GUI units are represented separately. GUI warps convert directly to window points, avoiding the old integer bottom-origin round trip.

A mouse accessor updates the native coordinates immediately before the OS warp; rendering a controller container uses the scene pointer directly for highlight and carried-item alignment even if an OS callback is delayed.
Container origins are synchronized after initialization and before input. Resizing preserves the hovered slot and suppresses fake movement from changed coordinate metrics.
Actual mouse clicks and scrolling switch to mouse input through Forge input events. Controller clicks continue through normal native menu transactions.

The standard profile uses the existing 640x480 GUI target and a centered uniform 720-scene fallback for intro/loading and menu anchors. It retains original available artwork and the native Java 1.17.1 panorama.

Standard crafting cycles the current variant in its center cell; standard pointer input uses the source 0.6 multiplier. HUD presets fit within the original 5% safe zone when a manually enlarged Java GUI is too small for the requested preset.
validation_limits: Native checks run on Linux/Mesa, with 2x Retina window-point/framebuffer metrics and delayed cursor callbacks simulated. The M1 Pro MacBook and its macOS/Temurin combination are not physically available in this workspace.
